card.name: Peak-concentration terms in drug interactions
card.fires_on: Words inside pharmacokinetic phrases such as Cmax and area under the curve, mostly the pieces C, max, or 'the' in 'area under the curve'. It appears in drug-interaction and exposure comparisons.

modes.label: Cmax pieces
modes.description: The C or max of 'C max' after a drug name or 'mean'.
modes.example: the mean<< C>> max and AUC values for glybur

modes.label: Area under the curve
modes.description: The word 'the' right after 'area under', before 'curve'.
modes.example: approximately a doubling of the maximum concentration (C max ) and area under<< the>> concentration versus time curve (AUC)

modes.label: Peak or exposure wording
modes.description: Words like peak or exposure in comparisons of drug levels.
modes.example: may result in lower<< peak>> concentrations and lower bioavailability than when used

card.writes: It suggests time-related or concentration-curve words coming next, as in time-course terms.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a drug-level sentence where the peak level or area under the curve is being named.
